summary: Tested the last untested boundary of the finding — that the defect needs the newest configuration entry to lie inside the replayed committed prefix — and reproduced it locally in both directions by adding a shallow case to the resurrect harness that omits the two client commits pushing the persisted commit index past the removal entry. With no extra commits (staged commit 5 against removal entry index 7) the restarted node keeps the committed two-server membership, does not resurrect the removed voter, reports one peer, and refuses the partitioned write; with the two extra commits the same harness reproduces the resurrection (three servers including the removed voter, two peers) and accepts the write. The revision is submitted as a successor of the current resurrect experiment with a fifth comparison asserting that the shallow case keeps the committed membership, so the 'at or below the persisted commit index' condition in the finding's trigger statement becomes execution-confirmed rather than reasoned, and the interpretation records the boundary as pending that receipt.
